title: A Noetherian complete local ring is a G-ring
statement: Let $(S,\mathfrak n)$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring which is complete, i.e. $\mathfrak n$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]: the canonical map $S\to\varprojlim_nS/\mathfrak n^n$ to its $\mathfrak n$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] is bijective. Then $S$ is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]: for every prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset S$ the completion map $S_{\mathfrak q}\to(S_{\mathfrak q})^\wedge$ is a regular ring map.

source.place: Proposition Tag 07PS (more-algebra-proposition-Noetherian-complete-G-ring, line 12356); complete local ring: algebra.tex Definition Tag 0324

proof.text: Apply isGRing_iff_pairsOfPrimes. For each q contained in p put B=S/q and P=p/q. The quotient is a domain because q is prime; the local and Noetherian quotient instances supply the other hypotheses. quotient_complete_local supplies maximal-ideal-adic completeness of B.

Apply complete_local_domain_finite_over_regular to B, obtaining a regular subring B0 over which B is finite, and its field-or-Cohen power-series presentation. Install the regularity and module-finiteness proofs as local instances.

Apply the regular power-series generic-fibre lemma at the contraction of P to B0, then the finite-subring generic-fibre ascent lemma with fraction field q.ResidueField. Mathlib supplies IsFractionRing B q.ResidueField. The resulting geometric regularity has the exact tensor product in the pairs-of-primes criterion. Its first conjunct supplies Noetherianity, so the criterion concludes IsGRing S.
